events.title: DEVBLOG 03 - "HOW HARD SHOULD IT BE?"
events.summary: Last time I wrote about making infection something you feel. This time it's the step before that: how hard each district should be in the first place."Too hard" depends on who's playing. Someone picking up the controls for the first time and someone chasing a stage 5 finish with every perk bought need very different things from the same district. events.title: AN UNREASONABLY LOGICAL DEMO
events.summary: The upcoming demo gives you seven districts and ten nights, with one deploy per night. The city starts at a 38.9% infection level, City Hall is completely overrun, and six of the seven districts are locked. Where do you go first? I didn't want to guess. So I deployed an algorithmic simulation paired with the game's rule set, the same code the demo runs - and had it play the ten nights over and over until it found the best route. events.summary: The challenge I’m working on right now is making district infection something you feel when you play. The map shows a percentage, but a higher number doesn’t yet mean a harder fight.I’m exploring two connected ideas: faster zombie spawns at higher infection levels, and adjusting how much infection each completed stage removes. events.title: CONTROLLER SUPPORT
events.summary: The (pre-release) demo now plays start to finish on a controller. Menus, the city map, all seven districts, the pause screen, the upgrade tree. No point where you have to reach for a keyboard or a mouse. That sounds like a small thing...but it wasn't, and the reason is worth writing down, because this game is not built the way most games are.
